From 15fe76e23615f502d051ef0768f86babaf08746c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 13:52:31 -0300
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/umem: Fix truncation for block sizes >= 4G

When the iommu is used the linearization of the mapping can give a single
block that is very large split across multiple SG entries.

When __rdma_block_iter_next() reassembles the split SG entries it is
overflowing the 32 bit stack values and computed the wrong DMA addresses
for blocks after the truncation.

Use the right types to hold DMA addresses.

Link: https://patch.msgid.link/r/1-v1-88303e9e509f+f7-ib_umem_types_jgg@nvidia.com
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: a808273a495c ("RDMA/verbs: Add a DMA iterator to return aligned contiguous memory blocks")
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/core/iter.c b/drivers/infiniband/core/iter.c
index 8e543d100657..3ed351e8fcf6 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/core/iter.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/core/iter.c
@@ -19,8 +19,8 @@ EXPORT_SYMBOL(__rdma_block_iter_start);
 
 bool __rdma_block_iter_next(struct ib_block_iter *biter)
 {
-	unsigned int block_offset;
-	unsigned int delta;
+	dma_addr_t block_offset;
+	dma_addr_t delta;
 
 	if (!biter->__sg_nents || !biter->__sg)
 		return false;
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a truncation bug in the RDMA `iter.c` file that occurs when the IOMMU creates a single large block spanning multiple scatter-gather (SG) entries. The root cause is the use of 32-bit `unsigned int` variables to store DMA addresses, which overflow when the block size is 4GB or larger, leading to incorrect DMA address calculations for subsequent blocks.

**File modified:** `drivers/infiniband/core/iter.c`

**Changes:**  
In function `__rdma_block_iter_next()`, two local variables were changed from `unsigned int` to `dma_addr_t`:
- `block_offset` — used to track the offset within the current SG block.
- `delta` — used to compute the distance to the next block boundary.

**Relationship:**  
Both variables are used together to reassemble split SG entries into contiguous memory blocks. By changing them to `dma_addr_t` (which is wide enough to hold any valid DMA address, typically 64 bits), the arithmetic no longer overflows, ensuring correct block iteration for arbitrarily large DMA mappings. This fix directly addresses the overflow condition described in the commit message.
